essentials: The LkSG obliges large companies in Germany to **manage human-rights and certain environmental risks** in their own business and at their **direct suppliers**.
It applies to companies with **at least 1,000 employees in Germany**. There is no turnover threshold.
It is in a **transition**: the reporting duty is being abolished, and the act will be replaced by the German law transposing the CSDDD.
Until a new law is in force, the **duties of care continue** and the authority can still act.

sections.title: Why it exists
text: Germany first tried a voluntary approach. When monitoring showed that too few companies met the expectations of the national action plan on business and human rights, the legislator made due diligence mandatory in 2021. The LkSG was one of the models for the EU's CSDDD.

sections.title: Who is covered
points: Companies of any legal form with their head office, principal place of business, administrative seat or a branch in Germany.
**At least 1,000 employees in Germany** since 2024. Employees of all German group companies are added up at the parent; temporary agency workers count after six months.
Suppliers are not covered themselves, but covered customers pass requirements on through contracts.

sections.title: The duties
steps: **Risk management** with clear responsibility, for example a human rights officer.
**Risk analysis** once a year and when circumstances change, for the own business and direct suppliers.
**Preventive measures**: purchasing practices, supplier selection, contractual assurances, training, controls.
**Remedial action** when a violation has occurred or is imminent.
**Complaints procedure** open to people along the supply chain.
**Indirect suppliers**: act when there is substantiated knowledge of a possible violation.
after: Like the CSDDD, this is an obligation to make appropriate efforts, not to guarantee a result.

sections.title: What is protected
text: The act refers to a list of international conventions. The human-rights risks include child labour, forced labour, unsafe working conditions, disregard of freedom of association, discrimination, withholding of an adequate wage, and unlawful eviction. The environmental risks are narrower than in the CSDDD: mercury, persistent organic pollutants and the export of hazardous waste.

sections.title: Enforcement
text: The Federal Office for Economic Affairs and Export Control, BAFA, supervises compliance. It can request information, order measures and impose fines of up to €8 million, or up to 2% of worldwide turnover for companies above €400 million. Companies fined heavily can be excluded from public contracts. The act creates no civil liability of its own.

sections.title: Where the reform stands
points: **Reporting**: BAFA stopped checking the annual reports. A bill that deletes the reporting duty and limits fines to serious violations was adopted by the cabinet in September 2025 and had its first reading in January 2026; the final vote was still outstanding when this page was reviewed.

**Replacement**: on 2 July 2026 the coalition announced that the CSDDD will be transposed one-to-one and that the scope of the LkSG is to be narrowed in advance. A draft for that had not been published at the time of review.
**Consequence**: companies between 1,000 and 5,000 employees would fall out of scope once the new thresholds apply. Until then the current text binds them.

mistakes.right: It is still in force. Only the checking of reports has stopped, and the amending law has not been passed.

mistakes.wrong: The act covers the whole supply chain equally.
mistakes.right: Regular duties cover the own business and direct suppliers. Indirect suppliers come in only with substantiated knowledge.

mistakes.wrong: Affected people can sue under the LkSG.
mistakes.right: It is enforced by BAFA. It creates no new civil liability.

practice: **Count employees in Germany** to establish whether the act applies to you directly.
**Keep the risk analysis and complaints procedure running** during the transition.
**Document decisions**, even though reports are no longer checked.
**Answer customer requests consistently**: one set of evidence for all customers under the act.
**Follow the reform**: the amendment bill and the CSDDD transposition draft.

quiz.q: Which threshold decides whether a company falls under the LkSG?
quiz.why: The LkSG counts employees in Germany and has no turnover test. The 5,000 and €1.5bn thresholds belong to the CSDDD.

quiz.q: For which part of the supply chain do the regular duties apply?
options: The own business and direct suppliers
All suppliers down to raw materials
quiz.why: Indirect suppliers are covered only when the company has substantiated knowledge of a possible violation.

quiz.q: What is the status of the reporting duty in autumn 2026?
options: No longer checked in practice; its formal abolition is still in Parliament
Replaced by the CSRD report by law
quiz.why: BAFA has stopped checking reports. The bill deleting the duty has not had its final vote.
